messages:
sophia: Quick report: ran into an odd auth/config behavior when running multiple AsyncClient instances in the same process while we have env-file rotation enabled. One client created with explicit api_key keeps getting overridden by the env key after rotation.

kevin: ouch. is that the same singleton-auth-provider thing we fixed last quarter?

sophia: looks related but not identical. I dug in: redwood.auth exports get_default_provider() that lazily creates a provider and the env-watcher mutates that provider's .api_key on file change. clients constructed afterwards pick up the latest, but clients constructed with explicit api_key still appear to use the provider value for outgoing requests (tested with http logs).

dan: can you paste a minimal repro?

sophia: sure, minimal async repro below. you can hit it by toggling the env file during the gather window.

```py
# repro_env_rotation.py
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def do(name, client):
    resp = await client.generate("hello")
    print(name, resp)

async def main():
    a = AsyncClient()                # reads env-watcher
    b = AsyncClient(api_key="sk-b") # explicit
    await asyncio.gather(do('A', a), do('B', b))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    asyncio.run(main())
```
kevin: what did the logs show?

sophia: logs show both requests with Authorization: Bearer env:sk-rotated-xyz, even though B was constructed with sk-b.

alex: that implies the client request pipeline uses module-level provider state rather than per-instance provider or injected header.

dan: is this on v0.12.3? any env var like REDWOOD_AUTH_PROVIDER set?

sophia: v0.12.3. no special env vars. I replicated locally and in CI.

kevin: proposed fix: make AsyncClient accept an optional AuthProvider (typed) and if api_key is passed, instantiate an internal provider bound to that key. If no provider passed, create one at instance init that subscribes to watcher events for that instance only. Avoid mutating module-level provider after bootstrap.

alex: +1. also, we should add typing for AuthProvider in client __init__ signature so mypy users get correct autocomplete. right now provider: Any in stub.

dan: we should add a small API helper: AuthProvider.from_env_watcher(shared=false) or maybe .shared() to opt into global behavior. default should be instance-isolated. Need a migration note.

kevin: can someone open an issue/PR? add a test that mocks the watcher and flips callbacks to ensure provider per-instance remains stable. don't toggle real files in unit tests.

sophia: will open issue + PR. I can write the test using monkeypatch and a fake watcher event. Test file suggestion: devex/tests/test_env_rotation_isolation.py. Test will create two clients, call generate concurrently, then call watcher callbacks and assert headers per request.

alex: small DX ask: can we document credential precedence in README (env, explicit param, AuthProvider) and show examples for multi-client processes? New users keep tripping over this.

ci-bot: Created issue #4151: "env-watcher rotation can overwrite explicit per-client api_key due to shared auth provider" and added label devex/bug. Assigned to @sophia.

kevin: thanks. FYI, add typing changes to mypy/py.typed and update stubs in types/redwood.pyi. This will reduce confusion that leads to bad usage.

dan: also flag this in release notes as a behavioral fix: "Auth provider is now instance-scoped by default; pass AuthProvider.shared() to opt into global rotation."

sophia: PR opened: draft #4152 with failing test + proposed fix. pinging for review. I'll include a short migration section in CHANGELOG.

alex: great, thanks for doing the reproduction and test. small follow-up after merge: add an example in examples/multi_client_rotation.py so customers can see proper patterns.

sophia: will do. marking thread blocked on review.
